clue.text: Is city covered in seaweed? That's a joke

indicators.note: one thing covered in another sits inside it, so the seaweed word wraps the other letters

parts.note: wrack is seaweed washed up on the shore
taken as written
EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether a town lies buried under seaweed, offered as a quip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' puts IS and EC inside WRACK. 'the city' in crosswords is often the City of London, whose postcode is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a quick witty remark, which is one kind of joke.

clue.text: Came first, lapping me in half of our race

indicators.note: lapping means wrapping round, so the winning word goes around the other

parts.note: won means came first
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner boasts of winning, lapping the narrator halfway round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lapping' puts ME inside WON. 'Our race' is the human race, not a running race.
explanation.definitionFit: Females make up about half of humankind, so they are half of our race.

clue.text: Clunky batteries spoiled child's favourite recourse

indicators.note: spoiled suggests damaged out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's clunky toy batteries have failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges CLUNKY BATTERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A security blanket is a familiar comfort object a child turns to for reassurance.

clue.text: Walk through East End, having weapon

parts.note: to cross is to walk through or over
Bow is a district in London's East End

explanation.surface: Someone crosses the East End with a weapon on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district in the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a weapon firing bolts from a bow mounted on a stock.

clue.text: Radioactive element at home in a flap

indicators.note: in signals insertion, one piece placed inside the other

parts.note: a state means a flap, a fluster
in means at home

explanation.surface: A radioactive substance in the house is causing panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a flap' and 'in a state' both mean flustered; IN goes inside A STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a rare radioactive chemical element, number 85.

clue.text: Genuine Greek island given to some girl

parts.note: Kos is an island in the Dodecanese
her refers to a particular girl

explanation.surface: A Greek island is presented to a certain girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Kosher, beyond its food sense, informally means genuine or legitimate.

clue.text: Sort of sugar runs short in class

indicators.note: running short of something means lacking it, so one letter is dropped from the sugar

parts.note: caster is a finely ground sugar used in baking
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A recipe note: one kind of sugar is in short supply in the kitchen class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs short' tells you to drop R, the cricket abbreviation for runs, from CASTER. Caster sugar is the British name for superfine sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in the Hindu system.

clue.text: Be upset about European and American being rich and white

indicators.note: about means around, so the weeping word goes round the rest

parts.note: to cry is to be upset

explanation.surface: Someone frets over Europeans and Americans being wealthy and white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E and AM inside CRY. The surface reads as social comment; the definition is about food or colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something creamy is rich and pale like cream, as a sauce or a colour.

clue.text: Miss appointment with firm an average joker

parts.note: to stand someone up is to miss a date with them
Co is short for company, a firm
the median is a kind of average

explanation.surface: Someone skips a meeting with a firm and a rather ordinary comic.
explanation.walkthrough: To stand up someone is to fail to turn up for a date with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up comedian is a comic who tells jokes on stage, so a professional joker.

clue.text: The privation of polar exploration

parts.note: the hardship explorers bear in polar cold calls for a quality of stamina, and Shackleton's ship on his Antarctic expedition bore that very name

explanation.surface: A remark on the hardships of exploring the poles.
explanation.walkthrough: Shackleton's ship on his 1914 Antarctic expedition was named Endurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to bear hardship, which is what polar explorers need.

clue.text: Farm of mine goes to solver's brother

parts.note: my means belonging to me
a croft is a small farm, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: A small farm of mine is handed over to a puzzler's sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver here is Sherlock Holmes, the great solver of mysteries; his older brother is Mycroft.
explanation.definitionFit: Mycroft Holmes is the elder brother of the detective Sherlock Holmes in Conan Doyle's stories.

clue.text: Attendant set out room with beds

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hospital ward is a room with beds for patients

explanation.surface: A hotel attendant lays out a room fitted with beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to STE, then WARD follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an attendant who looks after passengers on a ship, plane or train.

clue.text: Fatally, they're Scandinavians, and not Poles

parts.note: nor means and not
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A grim remark about some Nordic people, adding that they are not Polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality, but it is the two magnetic poles, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth three women of fate spin the destinies of gods and humans, so they rule fate and are Scandinavian.

clue.text: I had men join the marines in month of revolution

parts.note: taken as written
RM stands for the Royal Marines
I'd is short for I had
OR stands for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone describes recruiting men to join the marines during a revolutionary month.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go into the grid in a different order from the clue: THE, RM, I'D, OR. OR, for 'other ranks', is the usual crossword abbreviation for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermidor was the eleventh month of the French Revolutionary calendar, falling in midsummer.

clue.text: Group with empty beer glass, one crucial to serve

parts.note: a set is a group of things

indicators.note: the pint glass is taken with the empty sign held inside it

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
O, the zero, stands for empty or nothing

explanation.surface: A gang sit round an empty pint, waiting for whoever's turn it is to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' gives O, the figure for nothing, which goes inside PINT to make POINT. The definition plays on serving in tennis rather than at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a set point is the rally that can win the set, so the server's play is crucial there.

clue.text: Hears bugs scurrying round shrubs in Nevada

definitions.note: the answer word serves as a plural for these desert plants

indicators.note: scurrying round suggests letters dashing into new places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hears insects running about in the desert scrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scurrying round' rearranges HEARS BUGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagebrush is the aromatic shrub covering much of the deserts of Nevada.

clue.text: Why one uses pencil in championship?

definitions.text: Why one uses pencil in championship?

parts.words: Why one uses pencil in championship?
parts.note: read the question as a reason: a person writes in graphite because they have nothing to write with in ink; the same word names a golf or tennis tournament anyone may enter

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why a competitor in a tournament writes with a pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after its first letter: a zero, then the ink writing tool, so having none of the latter is why someone reaches for a pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: An open is a championship anyone may enter, such as the British Open in golf.

clue.text: Flipping Game Boy -— I would secure a type unable to adapt

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it in, so the extra letter goes inside
flipping turns the pieces over, reading them backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
a son is a boy
I'd is short for I would

explanation.surface: A Game Boy is flipped over and someone vows to grab one type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reverses RU, SON and ID to give DINOSUR; 'secure' puts A inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a dinosaur is a person or thing too old-fashioned to adapt, like the extinct reptiles.

clue.text: Fellow training monkey

parts.note: a fellow is a man
drill is training by repeated exercises

explanation.surface: A man trains a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large West African monkey with a brightly coloured face.

clue.text: No Jew eats British fish

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it inside, so the British letter goes within

parts.note: goy is a Yiddish word for someone who is not Jewish

explanation.surface: A gentile dines on fish caught in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' puts B inside GOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A goby is a small spiny-finned sea fish found in coastal waters.

clue.text: Garment's small opening kept one cooler, just about

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it, so the opening wraps the rest

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about here signals a turn, so the cooler is read backwards

parts.note: a fan cools the air

explanation.surface: A dress with a little vent let in some cooling air, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just about' turns FAN into NAF; 'kept' puts I and NAF inside PORE. The 's is 'has', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless dress or apron worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Intensity of fighting regularly voided match

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: every other letter is emptied out, leaving alternate ones

explanation.surface: The fierceness of a fight leaves a match regularly abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly voided' keeps the odd letters of MATCH, MTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth can mean intensity of feeling or ardour.

clue.text: Second dwarf gets closer

parts.note: titch is British slang for a very small person

explanation.surface: Another small person draws nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' looks like 'nearer' but means something that closes; a stitch closes a wound. Titch is British slang for a tiny person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is something that closes, pulling the edges of a wound or seam together.

clue.text: Foolish rabbi not a senator

indicators.note: foolish suggests silly or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious teacher acting the fool is clearly no politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolish' rearranges RABBI and NOT A. Brabantio is the Venetian senator, Desdemona's father, in Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello Brabantio is a senator of Venice and the father of Desdemona.

clue.text: Turning blue, left to linger

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: blue can mean smutty or indecent, which is lewd

explanation.surface: Someone going blue with cold is told to stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses LEWD to DWEL; L follows. 'Blue' as in blue jokes, rude ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell on something or in a place is to linger or stay there.

clue.text: Sell a German bottled drink

indicators.note: bottled means kept inside, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: Someone sells a German a bottled drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottled' points to the letters sitting inside 'Sell a German'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a common drink, particularly associated with Germany.

clue.text: Not starting free trip one elected to take part in? That's shabby

indicators.note: taking part in something puts one inside it, so the elected member goes within
the first letter of the trip word is dropped

parts.note: a junket is a trip paid for by others, often public funds
an MP is a Member of Parliament, someone elected

explanation.surface: Suggests a politician enjoyed a free jaunt and turned up looking scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not starting' drops the J of JUNKET to give UNKET; 'to take part in' puts MP inside it. MP is a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt means untidy or uncared for in appearance, the same as shabby.

clue.text: Stopping a huge meal half-eaten

indicators.note: something eaten by another goes inside it, so the half meal sits within

parts.note: big means huge

indicators.note: half of the six-letter meal word is kept, its last three letters lost

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: Someone stops partway through a vast meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' cuts DINNER to DIN; 'eaten' puts DIN inside BIG, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Abiding and stopping both mean staying or remaining in a place, as in an old sense of stop.

clue.text: Shade a problem for lawn when temperature first drops

indicators.note: the first letter falls away, so the opening T goes

parts.note: thatch is a mat of dead grass that troubles lawns

explanation.surface: Gardening advice on shading a lawn problem as the weather cools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when temperature first drops' removes the T at the front of THATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To hatch is to shade a drawing with fine parallel lines.

clue.text: Less easy to hold nothing back, for man of principle

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it

parts.note: harder means less easy

indicators.note: back means read backwards

parts.note: nil is nothing

explanation.surface: It is tougher to keep nothing in reserve if you are a principled man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NIL into LIN; 'to hold' puts it inside HARDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner sticks rigidly to principles and refuses compromise.
